ontology.Primitive: Smallest irreducible unit of capability the substrate understands (Signal, Operation, WorkPacket, Approval, Proof, Trace). Lives in L2 (substrate/types.py). Never projection-specific.
ontology.Invariant: The part of a repeatable pattern that must NOT change across instances — the contract that makes proof transferable (e.g. 'pending row may only transition via atomic status-claim').
ontology.Variable: The declared, typed slots a template exposes for instantiation (action_type set, target table, approval principal, projection_id, tenant_id). Everything tenant/projection-specific enters ONLY through variables.
ontology.RealityTemplate: f(invariants, variables, context) — a named, versioned, provable pattern: primitives composed under invariants with declared variables. Compiled once, instantiated many times.
ontology.TemplateInstance: One binding of a RealityTemplate's variables for one tenant+projection, with its own proof record.
ontology.TemplateGraph: A DAG of TemplateInstances where one instance's proof/context output feeds the next instance's variables. Workflows ARE TemplateGraphs.
ontology.TemplateEdge: A typed connection: (producer_instance, proof_field) -> (consumer_instance, variable). Edges carry proof, never raw trust.
ontology.ProofRequirement: What a template demands before its instance may be marked complete: envelope ids, server-truth reads, row verification, gate output. No proof, no completion.
ontology.CapabilityRevision: The learning edge: a completed instance's proof + defects found feed a revision of the template (invariant sharpened, variable added, gotcha recorded). Templates only improve through executed instances.
essentialism_rules: One canonical home per durable capability — duplicates must be classified (substrate/projection/template) or converged.
A template is only created from a pattern that has EXECUTED at least once with proof (no speculative templates).
A template with one instance is a record; extraction into an abstraction requires a second real instance (N>=2 rule).
Instance values (tenant, node, brand) never appear in template bodies — only in variable bindings.
Every template names its ProofRequirement; instances without proof cannot feed TemplateEdges.
